articleBody:
Before having tile laid on your lower-level concrete floor, running through a systematic checklist ensures your investment will not suffer from moisture debonding, cracking, or hollow sounds down the road. 

- [ ] ASTM F2170 moisture test reading under 75% RH — High internal moisture prevents standard thin-set mortars from bonding properly and signals the need for specialized moisture mitigation.
- [ ] Active water intrusion inspection completed — Finish tile should never be installed over weeping foundation seams, active leaks, or untreated drainage problems.
- [ ] Visual crack mapping across the slab — Shrinkage or settling cracks must be identified so crack-isolation membranes can be planned to prevent telegraphing into the tile.
- [ ] Surface flatness measurement with a straightedge — Lower-level slabs with severe dips require self-leveling underlayment to avoid tile lippage and uneven joints.
- [ ] 48 to 72 hour material acclimation period scheduled — Setting materials, membranes, and tiles must equalize with basement humidity and temperature before installation starts.
- [ ] Moisture-compatible mortar and grout verified — Using standard interior mortars over damp-prone slabs often leads to premature adhesive failure.
- [ ] Tile slip-resistance rating checked — Basements benefit from textured or slip-resistant tile finishes to keep the space safe if condensation occurs.
- [ ] Expansion gap perimeter planned — Leaving perimeter clearance along foundation walls accommodates seasonal structural contraction and expansion.

What to Prepare Before You Start
Review this list before your initial site assessment so you can point out past damp spots or recurring cracks directly to your contractor. If your basement needs concrete leveling, crack repair, or expert tile installation, contact Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866.
